limit-sinc.question: What does $\dfrac{\sin x}{x}$ get close to as $x\to0$? (Angles are in radians.)
limit-sinc.explanation: The fraction is $0/0$ at $x=0$, so it has no value there, but near 0 the values are close to 1: about $0.9983$ at $x=\pm0.1$ and $0.99998$ at $x=\pm0.01$. For small $x$ we have $\sin x\approx x$. A limit only looks at the values near 0, not at 0 itself.

limit-abs.question: What happens to $\dfrac{|x|}{x}$ as $x\to0$?
limit-abs.explanation: For $x>0$ we have $|x|/x=1$, and for $x<0$ we have $|x|/x=-1$. The right-hand limit is 1 and the left-hand limit is $-1$. A two-sided limit exists only when both sides agree, so there is no limit.
